title.narrative: Integrated Lifesaving support to contested areas in Alamata corridor

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThe proposed integrated Lifesaving Support to Contested Areas in the Alamata Corridor Project utilizes an intersectoral approach, integrating Nutrition, Health, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), and Education Assistance to significantly provide integrated services to the affected population. To ensure high-quality service delivery across the Seven targeted Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs) in these Woredas, the project will deploy a team consisting of a Health and Nutrition Coordinator, a Health Officer, and a Nutrition Officer. To implement other components of the project, Emergency WASH Officers (1 engineer and 1 environmental officer), three Education in Emergency (EiE) Officers, a Response Coordinator, an EiE Coordinator, and a Driver will be assigned. This team will focus on leading and coordinating the implementation of this integrated project. The health component of this project will strengthen the health system through the deployment of a Mobile Health and Nutrition Team (MHNT), rehabilitating damaged health facilities, and providing capacity-building training for health professionals.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe nutrition intervention of this project is also planned to strengthen community-originated nutrition responses and establish or enhance Stabilization Centers (SCs). The major key strategic activities for this nutrition intervention include the protection and support of safe and appropriate feeding for infants and young children to safeguard their survival, health, and growth. It also aims to protect, promote, and support Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) programs through the establishment of Mother-to-Mother Support Groups (MtMSGs). These groups play a crucial role in transmitting IYCF messages and converting them into practice and will enhance the effectiveness of Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM)-led Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) management, micronutrient supplementation, and practices, integrating all project components effectively on the ground. ltbrgtWASH elements are critical to the project’s success. At the household level, WASH Non-Food Items (NFIs), such as clean water containers (jerry cans), soap, and sanitation supplies, will be distributed. The project will emphasize hygiene and sanitation promotion through community engagement and capacity-building training to improve local practices.ltbrgtIn the education sector, the project will work to create access to non-formal and informal education, including providing training for teachers on pedagogical and related topics. A robust Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) system will be employed to track and evaluate the distribution of all items and services, ensuring that the needs of target populations are effectively met.ltbrgtWorld Vision Ethiopia (WVE) will collaborate closely with the appropriate Regional Health Bureau (RHB), the Nutrition Cluster, the Health Cluster, the WASH Cluster, the Education Cluster, and other relevant stakeholders, including the Water Bureau, the Education Bureau, and local partners who have an active presence in the target areas. ltbrgtTimely delivery of essential nutrition materials and supplies-including therapeutic supplies, nutrition registers/booklets, Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) cards, Information, Education, and Communication/Behavior Change Communication (IEC/BCC) materials, anthropometric equipment, and stationery will be ensured. All distributions and activities will adhere to the health tier system and other clusters’ standards in the targeted Woredas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
